Five of the six species tested avoided nose touch in much the same way (Figure 5A). The exception was *C. tripartitum*. After the first few positive trials, its overall avoidance rate fell below 10%, which suggests this species adapts to the stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the others (Figure 5A). The alitrunk (Fig. 15) is conspicuously swollen and sits well above the level of the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum bears a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove. The metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, leaving a short posterior face. The anterior and dorsal surfaces of the postpetiole form a single convexity, and its posterior face is truncated. Seen from above, the petiolar and postpetiolar nodes are both broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. These rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, though it typically carries 1–2 fine rugulae running across its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture continues around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured or show only the faintest superficial traces. The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiolar dorsum is rugulose. The postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured, and the gaster is unsculptured. Fine, acute hairs densely cover all dorsal surfaces of the head and body. Color varies from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

**A New Frontier in Wikitravel Data Representation**

Some of our data representations will be unique to Wikitravel, and no other organization will use them. The Turtle RDF standard is what makes this workable.

Turtle lets us write our own RDF schemas directly. We can develop those schemas with the same wiki techniques we already use, so we don't need a separate platform.

We can build a schema on our shared Wikitravel site at **Shared:Wikitravel:Schema**. Once it exists, its elements can be referenced in Turtle with the namespace **wts:** (Wikitravel schema).

This gives wiki data a structure that can grow with the site. #Wikitravel #RDF #DataScience #Technology

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Below is a summary of what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts are expressed very early in development (Figure 2). In the male, foxl2a expression was highly restricted. The diverged paralog, foxl2b, was present in most of the adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b expression was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill and ovary. Expression of foxl2b in the testis was very strong. This fits with previous work showing foxl2b present and foxl2a absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

These results suggest that foxl2b may be a critical regulator of male-specific genes such as cyp19b1, particularly later in development.

Thank you for your time and interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation based on the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), and from it obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). At leading order, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have a significant effect, while the slope-squared terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE drops, which gave us a uniform model.

We then built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. The uniform model generally captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. Over sinusoidal beds, its results match experimental data more closely than those of other established models. Over man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree with experimental data better than Kirby (1986) does.

An important use of the FEM model is predicting how waves transform over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot support a claim of carbon neutrality for electricity use beyond what the claimant actually consumes on its meters. Most RECs come from projects that would have been financially viable without selling them. [10] Consequently, they lack additionality, which is the attribute that matters here. Additionality asks a counterfactual question: what would have happened under the status quo if the REC had never been bought or contracted? There are many frameworks for testing it, but they all come down to whether the project needed REC revenue to survive financially. Unless additionality has been verified, a REC cannot be treated as a real emissions offset.

Subject: A Note on the Enduring Legacy of Buraq

Dear Friend,

The world was once a blend of reality and myth. A clear line between the two appeared only with modern comparative biology. Science has still not abolished the liminal zone where a figure like Buraq lives. We need transitional objects like her to connect empirical knowledge with spiritual experience, two realms that seem to point in different directions.

In contemporary culture she bridges rationalist taxonomies and the leftover power of myth. Nowhere is this clearer than in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure of both piety and speed, keeps turning up as a patron saint. Airlines from Libya to Indonesia carry her name. So do bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Because Buraq is so fluid as an aesthetic and linguistic object, commerce can bend her to almost any use. She presides over wings and wheels, and she also sells plastic and PVC, heavy metal, heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

**MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld**

MapleStory has thousands of monsters. Here is a short breakdown of where they live and how to survive them.

**The Weak Monsters**: These are the most common enemies, and you'll find them near towns. They wander aimlessly and keep doing so even if you bump into them. If they hurt you, just take the damage.

**The Dangerous Ones**: The most lethal monsters live deep in dungeons.

**The Aggro Mechanic**: This one matters. Monsters usually roam without purpose, even when you collide with them. Attack one or cast a debuff on it, though, and you will "aggro" it. You now have its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

**Behavioral Pattern**: Most enemies attack by running into you again and again.

**The Best Strategy**: The simplest answer to these repeat attackers is to keep hitting them. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to hold them in place.

**Dodge Tactics**: Sometimes you'll need to jump over a monster to avoid its attack entirely.

For the complete list of monsters, see **MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list**.

Remember that aggro works both ways: hit a monster and it will come after you. Stay safe and keep attacking.

We'd like to share some information about how hearing develops early in life. Most children learn to speak within their first few years. Hearing impairment can keep a child from learning to speak, and it can also keep them from understanding speech.

A severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child's hearing loss is often noticed late. By then, trouble communicating may already have strained family life and slowed the child's social development. These problems are smaller when the child belongs to a Deaf community that uses sign language in place of spoken language (see our article on Deaf Culture).

Many developed countries test hearing in the newborn period so that a deaf child born to a hearing family is not cut off without anyone realizing it. Sign language is a complete means of communication, but literacy depends on understanding speech. In the vast majority of written languages, symbols stand for the sounds of words.

Someone who once heard well enough to learn to speak and read will keep the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too weak to make out voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely learns to read well (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that identifying hearing impairment early is the key to helping a child with very insensitive hearing learn spoken language. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

We hope this explains why early intervention matters so much. If you have any questions, please contact us.

Warm regards,

In the nervous system, **transduction** is the process of converting stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors turn physical or chemical inputs into electrical impulses, which then travel to the brain. This conversion is what lets those signals reach the nervous system as neural impulses.

The **visual system** shows how this works. In the retina, **rod and cone cells** link the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes one of these photoreceptors, it causes a conformational change in the protein **rhodopsin**. That molecular shift starts a cascade of events that changes the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient drops, the electrical signals sent to the brain drop with it. So **more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses**, and the brain uses this pattern to decode what the eye sees.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), usually just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, among them Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live in the region, far more than in Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Motorways are dense here, yet hitchhiking is hard because of the tangled network of minor roads. The main motorways through the region are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on those main motorways. The smaller roads carry very little transit traffic, so getting anywhere on them is extremely difficult. Germany is generally a good country for hitchhiking. The Ruhr Area is by far its worst part for it. Hitching inside the Ruhr is like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul: the cities are independent, but to a traveler they feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this information helps you plan a safe and enjoyable trip.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Below are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as the number of voxels multiplied by the volume of one voxel. This applies only when the compartment in question has a CT number above zero.

We computed the change in functional residual capacity caused by PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) as the difference in total gas volume across the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume in poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions under the same two conditions.

We also measured how gas volume changed after PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated regions alone, defined as those with CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

Following the method described in reference [21], we classified each patient's distribution of lost aeration (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is giving storytelling new room for immersion through electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. These games are the latest step in a decades-long line of electronic games that treat the player as an avatar in a gameworld and also as a co-author working alongside the original designers.

Location-aware interfaces let players bring places in the physical world into their gameworld, and bring the gameworld into those places. No interactive medium has done this before. Mobile games also give the player a hand in worldmaking, and they drop linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling that depends on how the player experiences place.

The idea of "author-player" worldmaking is not new. Mobile games carry it past the usual limits of video games. Because location-aware interfaces push worldmaking off the screen and into the physical world, they can use the player's sensory experience of real places as a storytelling tool.

In our essay, we lay out a theory of the storytelling potential specific to mobile games. We also describe what happened when we tried to put that potential to work by designing and building our hybrid-reality game, **University of Death**.
